title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Price increase (1.5%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $0.68 show 8-11% below baseline; noise-adjusted lift is negligible.

drivers.name: Supply delivery warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk; no historical data on impact, but plausible demand reduction.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 438.2. A 1.5% price increase to $0.68 is observed, but recent weeks at $0.68 (2026-09-28, 10-05) show no uplift (median 401, vs baseline 438.2), indicating price sensitivity. The planner note warns of a short delivery, suggesting supply constraint may reduce sales. No past event or promotion at this price has lifted demand. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is near zero. With no positive driver and a supply risk, a downward adjustment is warranted. Evidence is limited to one past price change and a single note, so confidence is low.

  shelf price: 0.68 (+1.5% vs regular price 0.67)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 312.6 - 556.1 | 10%-90%: 346.5 - 529.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
